pr_title: sql: retry more distributed errors as local
pr_body:
This PR contains a couple of commits that increase the allow-list of errors that are retried locally. In particular, it allows us to hide some issues we have around using DistSQL and shutting down SQL pods.

Fixes: #106537.
Fixes: #108152.
Fixes: #108271.

Release note: None

See also: [How To Investigate a Go Test Failure \(internal\)](https://cockroachlabs.atlassian.net/l/c/HgfXfJgM)

/cc @cockroachdb/kv @cockroachdb/server [This test on roachdash](https://roachdash.crdb.dev/?filter=status:open%20t:.*TestServerShutdownReleasesSession.*&sort=title+created&display=lastcommented+project) | [Improve this report!](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/tree/master/pkg/cmd/internal/issues) Jira issue: CRDB-30331
comments: This is a very similar failure mode to https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/107592.

Tagging @JeffSwenson for any help you might be able to offer. I guess my fix in https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/107727 was not right, though it does seem to have made it less flaky, possibly.

There are two servers at play here:

1. The `tenant` server that is created first and lives for the entire test. The test opens a sql connection to the `tenant`.
2. The `tmpTenant` server that is created, then drained, then stopped

We don't have a sql connection to `tmpTenant`, so the `tmpTenant` shutting down should not impact the query to the `tenant` server. I suspect the issue is the `tenant` server is scheduling a distsql flow on the `tmpTenant` while/after the `tmpTenant` is shutdown.

See https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/106537 and https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/107592 for similar issues.

cc: @yuzefovich as FYI

~Hm, I'd be surprised if a SQL pod of `tmpTenant` would be used for DistSQL planning by the SQL pod of `tenant`.~ Nvm, scratch that (I misunderstood that `tenant` and `tmpTenant` are SQL pods for the same tenant).

The fix to related issues #108336 doesn't resolve this, but I'll take a closer look.

> I suspect the issue is the `tenant` server is scheduling a distsql flow on the `tmpTenant` while/after the `tmpTenant` is shutdown.

I agree with this assessment - I think the `instancestorage.Reader` on the `tenant` SQL pod has stale information that there are two available instances, and it looks to be expected behavior given what we did in #99941. In particular, when draining `tmpTenant` pod, we remove the corresponding rows from `sql_instances` and `sqlliveness` tables, but the in-memory cache of `tenant` for that information isn't updated. Does this sound right @JeffSwenson? Do we want to force the cache refresh of all running SQL pods (perhaps synchronously)?

Alternatively, we can rely on the retry-as-local mechanism by increasing the allow-list of errors (in particular, we could retry all that have `rpc error` substring). I'll include that change into #108336 for the consideration.

I think the fix in https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/108336 is sufficient for now.

Long term shutting down a sql server should trigger a graceful drain for all DistSQL flows and connections. One option that @dt suggested was to put a draining state on the sql_instances row. There is a rangefeed over the sql_instances table, so waiting for a few seconds would be enough for most servers to pick up the state change.

Alternatively, once the server starts draining, the sql server could begin NACKing all DistSQL requests and send a drain notification to all open DistSQL peers. That combined with your change to retry dial errors would likely be enough to avoid this class of problem for all healthy shutdowns.

review_comments: I like the approach of tagging errors that occur during the dial flow. This is a robust way to handle issues that occur during start up, which is the most common case we have seen for Serverless.
